statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-114469 is tracked in GitLab work item https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/811 . Git apply rejects patches larger than about 1 GiB, but checked only the size of the patch text, which for a binary patch is compressed and encoded, so a binary patch that inflates to a very large size passed the check and crashed git apply with an out-of-bounds read. Upstream fixed it in Git 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1, 2.55.1 and 2.56.1, as the Git 2.50.2 release notes describe: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.50.2/Documentation/RelNotes/2.50.2.adoc . The fix is in commits https://github.com/git/git/commit/55c54fd375849d303ab71307fc8f79254877cc89 and https://github.com/git/git/commit/dee1bb2a9fc75c3a1f7f1c6aaf86ff2c038bd436 , which in apply.c reject a binary patch whose stated inflated size exceeds that limit. The 2.52.1-r0 build is Alpine's security upgrade to Git 2.52.1, which contains the fix: https://git.alpinelinux.org/aports/commit/?id=2f20de3527863b1b84f620fefe687921498e7240 . We checked /usr/bin/git, the program in the git package that contains this code, in both published builds, 2.52.0-r0 and 2.52.1-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64: 2.52.1-r0 contains the new error message "index entry path is too long (" from the same security release, and 2.52.0-r0 does not. Earlier builds of this owner predate the fix.

CVE-2026-114469 is tracked in GitLab work item https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/git/-/work_items/811 . Git apply rejects patches larger than about 1 GiB, but checked only the size of the patch text, which for a binary patch is compressed and encoded, so a binary patch that inflates to a very large size passed the check and crashed git apply with an out-of-bounds read. Upstream fixed it in Git 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1, 2.55.1 and 2.56.1, as the Git 2.50.2 release notes describe: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.50.2/Documentation/RelNotes/2.50.2.adoc . The fix is in commits https://github.com/git/git/commit/55c54fd375849d303ab71307fc8f79254877cc89 and https://github.com/git/git/commit/dee1bb2a9fc75c3a1f7f1c6aaf86ff2c038bd436 , which in apply.c reject a binary patch whose stated inflated size exceeds that limit. Debian's git 1:2.47.3-0+deb13u1 does not include it, and the Debian tracker lists trixie as vulnerable: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114469 . DHI backports the apply.c changes of both commits unmodified (their new tests need a test helper Git 2.47 lacks and are not carried). The fixed version is the first build that carries the backport, and its shipped changelog lists it. We compared the git package of the two builds in the DHI Debian repository, on amd64 and arm64, using the symbol tables in git-dbgsym: parse_binary_hunk() in /usr/bin/git grows from 963 to 1151 bytes on amd64 and from 952 to 1076 bytes on arm64 between the build before the fix and the fixed build. Earlier builds of 2.47.3-0+deb13u1 also predate the backport.
